system_prompt:
You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — Park Sterling Corporation realized record after merger into South State Corporation, ~3-5-year horizon (~2020-2022)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. Because Park Sterling Corporation deregistered
> at closing, there is no post-closing public 10-K filed under its own name; this
> sub-dossier searches the continuing acquirer's (South State Corporation) later
> annual reports for any separate disclosure of the acquired business. It contains no
> information about how the transaction was structured at closing.

## Public-reporting status after the transaction (feasibility-relevant)
- Park Sterling Corporation (CIK 0001507277) filed a Form 15-12B on December 11, 2017,
  certifying termination of its registration under Section 12(g) and suspension of its
  duty to file reports under Sections 13(a)/15(d), listing "None" as the approximate
  number of holders of record as of the certification date; the filing was signed by
  South State Corporation "as successor by merger to Park Sterling Corporation." [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-17-072745, Form 15-12B]
- A search of Park Sterling Corporation's EDGAR filing history for periodic reports
  finds no Form 10-K or Form 10-Q filed after its Q3 2017 Form 10-Q (filed 2017-11-03,
  before the November 30, 2017 closing); no periodic report covering any part of the
  ~2020-2022 outcome window exists under this registrant. [SRC: https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001507277&type=10-K]
- South State Corporation (CIK 0000764038) is a continuing SEC registrant and remains
  an active EDGAR filer, having filed Form 10-K annual reports covering fiscal years
  2020 (filed 2021-02-26) and 2021 (filed 2022-02-25), confirming the acquirer is an
  SEC/EDGAR filer whose later disclosures can be checked for separate treatment of the
  acquired business. [SRC: SEC accession 0001558370-21-001976, Form 10-K] [SRC: SEC accession 0001558370-22-002075, Form 10-K]

## Search for separate disclosure of the acquired business in the acquirer's later 10-Ks
- South State's Form 10-K for fiscal year 2020 (filed 2021-02-26) contains exactly two
  references to "Park Sterling," both in purchase-accounting comparative footnote
  tables covering fiscal years 2018-2019 (an accretable-yield roll-forward showing a
  "Park Sterling Corporation (Park Sterling) acquisition Day 1 adjustment" for 2018,
  and an other-real-estate-owned roll-forward showing amounts "Acquired in Park
  Sterling Corp. acquisition" in 2018); no fiscal-year-2020 line item or narrative
  discussion of the acquired Park Sterling business appears. [SRC: SEC accession 0001558370-21-001976, Form 10-K]
- South State's Form 10-K for fiscal year 2021 (filed 2022-02-25) contains no
  reference to "Park Sterling" anywhere in the filing. [SRC: SEC accession 0001558370-22-002075, Form 10-K]
- No separate disclosure of the Park Sterling business's post-close financial or
  operating trajectory (e.g., a segment-level scalar, a divestiture, an impairment
  specifically attributed to the acquired branches) was located in either 10-K within
  the ~2020-2022 outcome window. [UNVERIFIED]

## Items sought but not found
- No reputable-press source was located reporting a divestiture, closure, impairment,
  or comparable outcome scalar specifically attributed to the former Park Sterling
  branch network or customer base within the ~2020-2022 window, as distinct from South
  State's consolidated (multi-acquisition) results. [UNVERIFIED]
- South State completed at least one other acquisition (identified in the FY2020 10-K
  footnotes as "CSFL," closed June 2020) in the same window, meaning even South State's
  consolidated figures cannot be attributed to the Park Sterling business alone without
  a separate disclosure, which was not found. [SRC: SEC accession 0001558370-21-001976, Form 10-K]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- Because Park Sterling Corporation deregistered from SEC reporting effective its
  December 11, 2017 Form 15-12B, there is no public periodic-report record filed under
  its own name for the ~2020-2022 window. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-17-072745, Form 15-12B]
- South State Corporation, the surviving registrant, remains an active SEC filer and
  did file 10-Ks covering the outcome window, but a text search of those filings found
  no fiscal-year-2020 or fiscal-year-2021 disclosure isolating the acquired Park
  Sterling business's realized trajectory — only stale (2018-2019) purchase-accounting
  comparative footnotes referencing the original acquisition. [SRC: SEC accession 0001558370-21-001976, Form 10-K] [SRC: SEC accession 0001558370-22-002075, Form 10-K]
- Per the no-record convention, this case is coded **uncertain** on the outcome: the
  absence of any separate acquirer disclosure of the acquired business precludes a
  sourced determination of its realized 3-5-year trajectory.

[SLICE END]
